messages:
sara: Heads-up — saw an ArgoCD prune wave hang on the app-of-apps that manages gpu-pools. Several namespaces are stuck in Terminating and Argo refuses to progress, which is blocking the GPU node provisioning workflow after the latest terraform apply. Anyone seen this before? :thinking:

josh: Ugh. Can you paste the namespace state and the ArgoCD sync logs? root cause is often finalizers or an orphaned CRD.

sara: Paste of `kubectl get ns gpu-pools -o json` snippet:
```
"status": {"phase": "Terminating"},
"metadata": {"finalizers": ["helm.sh/release"], "annotations": {"owner": "app-of-apps/gpu"}}
```
Also ArgoCD shows `prune wave: waiting (child hanging)` in the app events.

ops-bot: ArgoCD: app gpu-pools-app sync failed. Reason: Prune blocked by terminating namespace. Details: https://argocd.internal/logs/....

liam: Finalizers from Helm release — probably helm deletion hook didn't finish. Quick fix is to remove the finalizer on the namespace to let prune continue, but we should be careful: that can orphan resources if helm didn't remove them.

josh: Agreed. Steps I propose: 1) quick patch to remove finalizer to let Argo continue, 2) run `helm list --all-namespaces` for charts in that ns, 3) re-run helm uninstall where appropriate, 4) add a pre-delete hook in the chart to clean up CRs.

sara: I'm fine to patch now if someone else is monitoring. Command I ran in staging successfully: 
```
kubectl patch ns gpu-pools -p '{"metadata":{"finalizers":null}}' --type=merge
```
Note: I removed only the problematic finalizer after confirming helm release was already absent.

devex-emma: Quick note on impact: because the autoscaler couldn't bind pods to GPU nodes, some jobs spilled to our fallback hosted instances and cost spiked. We should add a terraform check during deploy that validates namespace deletions and cloud GPU quota in target region before letting app-of-apps prune run.

liam: Also consider changing the app-of-apps sync strategy temporarily: disable automated prune or set smaller prune-wave concurrency so a single stuck child doesn't block the whole wave. We can add a flag on the app manifest to skip pruning while we fix infra.

josh: Follow-up: I patched the namespace, Argo resumed prune and completed. GPU pool helm-chart re-created nodepool resources and cluster autoscaler started provisioning again. Confirmed by `kubectl get nodes | grep gpu` on the cluster.

sara: Thanks — rolling incident notes: 1) root cause: leftover helm finalizer on namespace after partial uninstall, 2) immediate remediation: patch finalizer, 3) mitigation: add chart pre-delete cleanup + detect Terminating namespaces in pipeline + terraform region quota check, 4) follow-up ticket: ENGINFRA-327 to add alert and a safe automatic retry for prune waves.

devex-emma: I opened ENGINFRA-327 and linked cost spike details. cc @finance for visibility. :chart_with_upwards_trend:

josh: I'll also add a small runbook snippet in the Argo ops doc for "stuck prune wave due to namespace finalizer" with the safe commands and checks.

sara: Great, closing the thread — please DM if you see similar in other regions.
